title: ANZ profit up despite loan slump
full_text:
ANZ joined the big four banks in reporting a plunge in home loan application volumes since Jim Chalmer’s property investor tax grab, however its quarterly profit of $1.9bn (up 1 per cent) beat expectations.
ANZ told investors that home applications by value declined 12 per cent in the period from the federal budget to the end of July.
National Australia Bank, Westpac and Commonwealth Bank also copped a slide in mortgage applications since the Treasurer’s May budget changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax were announced. CBA, Australia’s biggest home lender, reported a 15 per cent drop in mortgage applications.
Cash return on tangible equity was broadly flat, impacted by a $NZ125m ($103m) expense provision following a May New Zealand class action ruling, which the bank has appealed.
ANZ chief executive Nuno Matos said the bank “continued to improve productivity, margins and business volumes, including accelerating growth in business banking and returning home lending to system growth”.
“We continue to watch the external environment closely across our network. Our balance sheet and capital position remain strong, and we are staying close to our customers should they need support,” Mr Matos said.
An organisational reset is on track, with 84 per cent of 3500 staff exiting the bank by the end of the quarter. About 73 per cent of estimated gross cost savings of $875m in FY26 were realised at the end of June.
Citi analysts Thomas Strong and Nilesh Bhaiya said the profit, about 2 per cent higher than consensus expectations, was aided by a bad debt charge of $102m, well below the run-rate estimated at $180m-$205m as non-performing loans were stable over the quarter. However, core earnings were 1 per cent below the consensus run-rate, but this largely reflected the class action provision. “Overall, we think the market should receive well the better performance on costs,” Citi said.
